questions.prompt: Calculate the Fourier sine coefficient \(b_3\) of \(f(x)=1\) on \((0,\pi)\), where \(b_3=\frac2\pi\int_0^\pi f(x)\sin(3x)\,dx\).
questions.answer:

Final answer: \(b_3=\frac{2(1-(-1))}{3\pi}\).

questions.prompt:
Part (a): Calculate \(\int_0^1 x^{13}\,dx\).
Part (b): Prove that \(\sin(mx)\) and \(\sin(nx)\) are orthogonal on \((0,\pi)\) for distinct positive integers \(m,n\).
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
\[\int_0^1x^{13}dx=\left[\frac{x^{14}}{14}\right]_0^1=\frac1{14}.\]
Final answer: \(1/14\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
Use \(2\sin(mx)\sin(nx)=\cos((m-n)x)-\cos((m+n)x)\). Both cosine integrals vanish because their integer frequencies are nonzero:
\[\int_0^\pi\sin(mx)\sin(nx)dx=0.\]
Final answer: \(\langle\sin(mx),\sin(nx)\rangle=0\) for \(m\ne n\).

questions.prompt:
Part (a): Calculate the Fourier sine coefficient \(b_15\) of \(f(x)=1\) on \((0,\pi)\), where \(b_15=\frac2\pi\int_0^\pi f(x)\sin(15x)\,dx\).
Part (b): Prove Parseval's identity for a finite orthonormal expansion \(f=\sum_{n=1}^N c_n\phi_n\).
questions.answer:
Part (a)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
\[b_15=\frac2\pi\left[-\frac{\cos(15x)}{15}\right]_0^\pi=\frac{2(1-(-1))}{15\pi}.\]
Final answer: \(b_15=\frac{2(1-(-1))}{15\pi}\).

Part (b)
We need to complete the requested calculation or proof.
Method: Apply the stated mathematical method and simplify each step.
\[\|f\|^2=\left\langle\sum_m c_m\phi_m,\sum_n c_n\phi_n\right\rangle=\sum_{m,n}\overline{c_m}c_n\delta_{mn}=\sum_{n=1}^N|c_n|^2.\]
Final answer: \(\|f\|^2=\sum_{n=1}^N|c_n|^2\).
